items.summary: Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen gave up five goals on 14 shots while Colton Ellis allowed three goals in relief on Wednesday.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Stephen R. Sylvanie Buffalo Sabres’ fans were witness to another difficult loss Wednesday night as the Tampa Bay Lightning defeated the home team 8-3. Nikita Kucherov recorded a hat trick and Brandon Hagel scored two goals of his own. Sabres goaltender Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen gave up five goals on 14 shots, while backup netminder Colten Ellis, who took over the crease less than two minutes into the third period, allowed three goals on just eight shots. On Thursday’s episode of Daily Faceoff LIVE , Tyler Yaremchuk and former NHL goaltender Carter Hutton discuss Buffalo’s goaltending woes and what the future holds for a team looking to earn another playoff berth this spring. Tyler Yaremchuk : UPL gets the start and gets yanked early in the third period after giving up five goals on 14 shots. Ellis comes in cold early in the third period … if you’re going to pull UPL, do it after the second period, don’t just do it one minute into the third period. Carter Hutton : It’s a tough spot to be in, but if you’re Ellis, this is what you have to do. When you have a chance to go in, you have to find a way to stop the bleeding. It’s a tough spot, but when you aren’t the guy, you aren’t the guy. In Buffalo, there’s probably a lot of concern with how this team is going. After you break that 14-year playoff drought, and now Alex Tuch and Bowen Byram are gone, you’re wondering what is this team? Are we back in the mix? It’s a tough Atlantic Division . Now, Connor Hellebuyck’s name has swirled around Buffalo since the summer, and all of a sudden, you see him be undefeated for the New Jersey Devils and you’re watching your goalies struggle to make saves. Among the players added for the event set to take place in Quebec next month are some U.S. National Team Development Program alums, including forward Jamie Glance. The New Hampshire native added another five points during the 2026 IIHF Under-18 Men’s World Championship, which saw the Americans get shockingly eliminated in the quarterfinals. The Boston University commit made the move to the QMJHL this season and has been fun to watch with the Saint John Sea Dogs. In 18 contests, the 18-year-old has nine goals and 14 assists for 23 points. Glance joins Carter Meyer and Levi Harper, who were previously named to the CHL’s roster, as former USNTDP stars who decided to join the major junior ranks before heading off to college. The trio will go up against some old friends, as the U.S. Under-18 Team looks to pick up their second victory in the showcase’s young history. The full CHL roster features 13 Canadians, four Americans, and three Russians, with defenseman Filip Kovalcik and goaltender Vilmer Salen Forsberg hailing from Slovakia and Sweden, respectively. items.title: Sedins unhappy with Canucks’ results, weighing options amid dismal season
items.body: Daniel and Henrik Sedin say they're not happy with the Vancouver Canucks ' results, but they believe in their coaching staff and players. The NHL team's co-presidents of hockey operations spoke to reporters on Thursday about the beleaguered club, which sits at the bottom of the league standings with a 3-16-1 record. The Canucks have lost six straight games and 16 of their last 17. Daniel Sedin says they're evaluating players every day but have yet to see the group put together a full, consistent effort over an entire game. His twin brother, Henrik Sedin, says Vancouver's front office is "looking at all players" to see what options are available for improving the team, but that the Canucks won't simply trade top talent away to get more draft picks because they need players who can produce on the ice and support up-and-coming athletes. The Sedins played their entire 17-season NHL careers in Vancouver and were appointed the team's co-presidents of hockey operations in May after the Canucks finished the 2025-26 season last in the league.

items.title: Canadiens’ Mike Matheson returns to lineup after six-game absence
items.summary: Matheson has been out of action due to a lower-body injury, though Montreal remains near the top of the Atlantic.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Talia Sprague-Imagn Images Some reinforcements are coming back to the Montreal Canadiens ahead of a thrilling matchup. On Thursday, the team announced that defenseman Mike Matheson will be back in the lineup for that night’s game, which will see the Canadiens pay a visit to the rival Boston Bruins. Matheson has been out of action for the past six games due to a lower-body injury, though it remains unclear when he was hurt. His last appearance came on Oct. 27, when he picked up two assists in a 2-0 victory over the St. Louis Blues . With Matheson out of the lineup, the Canadiens have done well, going 4-0-2, though the team lost to the Minnesota Wild in overtime this past Tuesday night. The 32-year-old has struggled to stay in the lineup this season, as he has missed a total of 10 games so far in 2026-27. Another lower-body injury led to him missing time in October as well. In his eight appearances this year, Matheson has scored one goal and three assists for four points, a little bit better than the scoring pace he has had over the past two seasons, which saw him score 31 points and 37 points in the 2024-25 and 2025-26 campaigns, respectively. The Quebec native is in his first season of the six-year contract extension he signed last November, which carries a cap hit of $6 million through the 2030-31 campaign. The Canadiens (11-3-4) are riding an 11-game point streak heading into Thursday night’s action. Montreal sits tied for second in the Atlantic Division with the Tampa Bay Lightning , one point back of the first-place Bruins.

items.summary: Will he or won’t he? The major storyline around the Minnesota Wild this season is whether or not their star defenceman will sign a new contract. Adam Vingan explores the team’s play through one quarter to examine if they’re standing out as a contender with Hughes.
items.body: The will-he-or-won’t-he drama surrounding Quinn Hughes ’ future with the Minnesota Wild rages on as the superstar defenceman still has not committed to the team past this season. items.summary: Hall reached the milestone during the Hurricanes’ Global Series game in Helsinki, Finland.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Carolina Hurricanes are squaring off against the Seattle Kraken in the first of two NHL Global Series games in Helsinki, Finland on Thursday afternoon, and it represents a major career milestone for one of their veteran players. Winger Taylor Hall, the No. 1 overall pick from the 2010 NHL Draft, appeared in his 1,000th career game in the NHL in the midst of his 17th career season. This is Hall’s 122nd game as a member of the Hurricanes after he was acquired from the Chicago Blackhawks in January of 2025. In the latest chapter of his career, Hall has been an excellent depth scoring piece for Carolina, and he was instrumental for the Hurricanes in capturing the Stanley Cup in 2026, the first of his career. Hall began his career as a beacon in the middle of the Decade of Darkness for the Edmonton Oilers , where he spent the first six seasons of his NHL career as part of a promising young core looking to turn things around. Just one year after Connor McDavid arrived in Alberta, the Oilers sent Hall to the New Jersey Devils in exchange for Adam Larsson in a trade that was infamously one-for-one . The Calgary native flourished with the Devils. After a solid but unspectacular 53 points in 72 games in his first season in Newark, Hall pieced together the best year of his career in 2017-18. On a New Jersey team that was largely devoid of offensive talent, Hall racked up 93 points in 76 games played, dragging the team into the Stanley Cup Playoffs and winning the Hart Trophy as the league’s MVP along the way. items.title: Senators’ Linus Ullmark to return after nine-game absence
items.summary: Ullmark suffered another lower-body injury last month, while Ottawa has held firm in the Atlantic Division.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Marc DesRosiers-Imagn Some reinforcements are returning to the nation’s capital. Following the team’s morning skate, it was revealed that Ottawa Senators goaltender Linus Ullmark has been activated from injured reserve and will be starting on Thursday night, when the Senators host the Colorado Avalanche. Ullmark has missed the past nine games due to a lower-body injury s uffered during a game on Oct. 21 against the Florida Panthers . He was quickly placed on IR, with Ottawa riding Samuel Ersson throughout his absence. Ullmark has missed the past nine games, with the Sens doing okay without him, going 4-3-2 after losing to the Washington Capitals this past Tuesday night. Yet, the Sens remain in the thick of the hunt for a Stanley Cup Playoff spot. The return of the Swedish backstop will certainly help Ottawa, as Ullmark has been exceptional in his limited action this year. In eight starts, he has posted a record of 7-1-0, with a 1.33 goals-against average and a .945 save percentage. His lone loss came at the hands of the Philadelphia Flyers back on Oct. 17. For Ottawa fans, seeing Ullmark injured has become the norm since he was dealt to the team in 2024. While he’s played at least over half of the games in each of his first two seasons, he has been on and off the injured list, along with taking a personal leave of absence last season. He’s already missed some time this year, as an injury against the Boston Bruins earlier this month knocked him out for one game. Yet, when he’s in between the pipes, few players have had a greater impact on the Sens than he. The Senators (11-6-2) are currently fourth in the Atlantic Division, two points ahead of the Panthers for the second Wild Card spot in the Eastern Conference.

In the same transaction, the Flames assigned Honzek to the Calgary Wranglers in the AHL. The reassignment will likely serve as a conditioning loan. It’s believed that he suffered his lower-body ailment in the Flames’ October 8th matchup against the Colorado Avalanche. The former 16th overall pick of the 2023 NHL Draft has been limited to four games this season after missing a month with injury. He wasn’t productive in those four contests, going scoreless with a -4 rating while averaging 15:39 of ice time per game. As a recent first-round pick, Calgary hoped Honzek would play a part in their rebuild. However, injuries are quickly becoming a recurring issue for the Trencin, Slovakia, native. Last season, after scoring two goals and four points in 18 games, Honzek’s season was prematurely ended after shoulder surgery. Still, given his age, he has more than enough time to develop into what the Flames believe he can be. items.title: Nikita Kucherov is red-hot since trade request
items.summary: Kucherov has racked up 11 points in the six games since it came out that he wouldn’t re-sign with Tampa.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Nick Wosika-Imagn Images Usually, when a player says that he wants to leave a team, he will sulk and trudge through games, or simply not play at all. It was just a couple of weeks ago that the Tampa Bay Lightning legend made a trade request, as he reportedly wouldn’t re-sign with the only team he has ever known. While the announcement sent shockwaves through the league, it did little to deter the 33-year-old’s play. In the six games since the news broke, Kucherov has been on fire, scoring five goals and 11 points across six games, including a hat trick against the Buffalo Sabres on Wednesday night. On Thursday’s edition of Daily Faceoff LIVE , Tyler Yaremchuk and Carter Hutton break down Kucherov’s incredible play since it came out that he wanted out of town. Carter Hutton: It’s been a show of talent so far, and I think this is one of those where you kind of kick the hornet’s nest, this is what you’re going to get. He was pretty clear about how he felt the way that he was treated, and it wasn’t about the money; it was about the disrespect. I think that factor is, now, he is playing with that edge and that fire, and there’s different players are motivated in different ways, and you have to find ways to do it. I think that’s what we’re seeing right now from Kucherov, is the fact that he’s motivated to be the best possible player that he can be, and to show BriseBois and his team he’s not turning on them, he’s not checking out, he’s just going to use this as fuel. Right now is a great example of a team that went into Buffalo and just absolutely waxed them last night. That is a big win and a statement win for the Lightning.

items.body: Register Login Morning Notes: Acciari, Cernak, Marchessault By Gabriel Foley | at November 12, 2026 8:30 am The Philadelphia Flyers lost forward Noel Acciari to an upper-body injury sustained during Wednesday night’s loss to the Edmonton Oilers. Acciari was injured when a trip from Oilers goaltender Tristan Jarry sent him hard into the boards. Jarry was assessed a minor penalty on the play. No details of Acciari’s injury have been revealed yet. Acciari recorded six minutes of ice time and no notable stat changes before going down with injury. He opened the game on Philadelphia’s fourth-line, though the absence of a right-wing led to expanded minutes for Flyers youngster Matvei Michkov . Playing more than 20 minutes, Michkov managed one assist in the two-goal outing. While an aptly timed promotion for the winger, Philadelphia will hope they aren’t without Acciari for long. The 35 year old has four points, 46 hits, and a 53.3 faceoff percentage through 21 games this season. Any absence as a result of this injury will be his first of the season.

items.title: Fan Fest provides entertainment for children at Global Series
items.summary: HELSINKI -- Hundreds of school children waited mostly patiently in line for the 2026 NHL Global Series Finland Fan Fest to open at Narinkka Square in Helsinki on Thursday.
items.body: More than 25 hockey-based activities bring joy during visit from Hurricanes, Kraken HELSINKI -- Hundreds of school children waited mostly patiently in line for the 2026 NHL Global Series Finland Fan Fest to open at Narinkka Square in Helsinki on Thursday. When they were given the go-ahead at 9 a.m., they flooded through the entrance to try the more than 25 hockey-based activities featured at the festival. The children were the initial visitors to the Fan Fest ahead of the first game between the Carolina Hurricanes and Seattle Kraken at Veikkaus Arena on Thursday (12 p.m. ET; HHN, Prime Video, CARNHL, KONG, NHLN, SN+, TVAS). About 4,000 school children from the Helsinki area are expected to visit the Fan Fest during special four-hour sessions Thursday and Friday that are closed to the public. "It's really to give them that great experience," NHL vice president of international operations Mark Black said. "For some of them, it's going to be their first experience with hockey, and we just want to make it a memorable experience for them. Obviously, for the teachers, it's a good opportunity to get the kids outdoors, looking for additional things, so we're always grateful for the schools and the teachers to bring their kids out. "For us, it's to give kids who know hockey the opportunity to engage with the NHL, but certainly for the kids who don't have hockey experience relevant to them, it gives them their first hockey experience." The Fan Fest is open to the public beginning at 4 p.m. local time Thursday and Friday and 12 p.m. local time Saturday leading up to the second game between the Hurricanes and Kraken (1 p.m. ET; HHN, Prime Video, CARNHL, KONG, KING, NHLN, SN1). items.title: ‘He’s a human CPU’: Meet Joey Cullen, the electric, high-flying 2028 NHL Draft superstar
items.summary: The son of three-time Stanley Cup champ Matt Cullen is looking to become the family’s biggest hockey star.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Steven Ellis Joey Cullen is going to get asked a lot of questions about his family’s hockey history. That comes with the territory – just ask Tij Iginla or Caleb Malhotra. Cullen’s family tree is especially impressive. His father, Matt, is a three-time Stanley Cup champion. Joey’s brother, Wyatt, was a top-10 pick by the Nashville Predators last year, and he’s expected to center USA’s top line at the World Juniors. And that’s only scratching the surface; multiple other family members ended up making the NHL as well. The 16-year-old was one of the top recruits for the U-17 USA Hockey National Team Development Program last spring. Many scouts viewed him as the premier offensive threat in the country, with a strong chance of going in the top five in 2028. It’s still exceptionally early, but Cullen hasn’t done anything to suggest it’s not a realistic prediction right now. Teams love players with NHL bloodlines. Not only did Cullen have his brothers to lean on, but he got to watch his father win two of his Stanley Cups with the Pittsburgh Penguins . Even at a young age, the experience – and getting to be close to players like Sidney Crosby and Evgeni Malkin – is something he’ll never forget. “It was unreal,” Cullen told reporters at the U-17 World Challenge last week, with about the biggest smile you’ll ever see. “I was super blessed to be able to be around a lot of great players and see what they do at the highest level.” That love for the sport blossomed, and Joey, like Wyatt, quickly became a top prospect in his age group. items.title: Sharks’ Celebrini fifth-youngest player in NHL history to reach 200 career points
items.summary: Sidney Crosby, Wayne Gretzky, Jimmy Carson and Mario Lemieux are the only players to hit the milestone at a younger age.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Bob Kupbens-Imagn Images Macklin Celebrini has found himself in rare air. During the San Jose Sharks ‘ 3-2 shootout loss to the Pittsburgh Penguins on Wednesday , Celebrini hit the 200-point milestone in his career, becoming the fifth-youngest player to reach that threshold. Celebrini achieved the feat midway through the third period of the game, when an offensive zone sequence saw Will Smith pass the puck across the zone to Michael Kesselring, who had previously pinched up on the breakout rush and was still deep in the zone. Kesselring immediately bumped the puck towards Celebrini in the high slot, who faked the first shot to trick the defense and goalie before firing home a goal to cut Pittsburgh’s 2-1 lead in half and giving him his 200th career point. Celebrini then followed it up with the primary assist on Mason Marchment’s game-tying goal with a bit over four minutes to go in the third period, giving him his 201st point. With his 200th point, Celebrini became the fifth-youngest player to reach the milestone, doing so at the age of 20 years and 151 days. He joins some elite players in the process, with the four players ahead of him being Mario Lemieux (20 years, 133 days), Jimmy Carson (20 years, 107 days), Wayne Gretzky (19 years, 347 days) and Sidney Crosby (19 years, 207 days). Admittedly, Celebrini and Crosby do have an advantage to get there in a similar amount of time to the likes of Gretzky and Lemieux, as the two have birthdays closer to the cut-off date for draft eligibility, with Celebrini’s being June 13th and Crosby’s being August 7th. Today, we look at three advanced stats storylines behind Connor McDavid’s historic start for the Edmonton Oilers. Connor McDavid is off to the best start of his illustrious NHL career for the Edmonton Oilers, and his advanced metrics are fueling what could be one of the highest-scoring seasons in history. The Oilers captain became the fourth different player in NHL history with a season-opening 20-game point streak, joining Wayne Gretzky (three times), Mats Sundin and Dany Heatley . It is McDavid's second career 20-game point streak (also 20 games in 2025-26) making him one of eight players ever and one of two active players (other: Patrick Kane ) with multiple point streaks of 20-plus games. McDavid previously became the fastest player in League history to reach 30 assists in a season (15 games), besting the previous mark set by Gretzky (16 games in 1984-85). He also became the fastest player to record 12 multipoint games in a season (17 games) since Peter Forsberg (17 games in 2005-06). The 29-year-old is on pace for 205 points in 84 games, which would challenge Gretzky's current single-season scoring record (215 in 1985-86). McDavid's highlight-reel goal 50 seconds into their game against the New York Rangers on Nov. 1, his franchise-record eighth opening-minute goal of his career, included a speed burst of 22.79 mph while skating through all three zones; it was the fastest burst resulting in a goal in the NHL this season. The 19-year-old needs two goals Thursday to get 30 for his career, which would tie Hockey Hall of Famers Brian Leetch and Phil Housley for the second most by a defenseman through 100 games in the NHL's modern era (since 1943-44), behind Mark Howe (31). It was also his 76th career point, which tied Rick Hampton for the fourth most in NHL history by a teenage defenseman on a list topped by Housley (132), Rasmus Dahlin (84) and Ray Bourque (79). items.title: Oilers beat Flyers in OT as goaltending shows signs of stability
items.summary: After consecutive wins where an Oilers goalie was the best player on the ice, it’s starting to look like Edmonton might finally have found some stability in the crease.
items.body: EDMONTON — Back in 1987, when the Edmonton Oilers would win a Stanley Cup off a season in which their team save percentage was .881, Grant Fuhr taught us that there was only one stat that truly mattered. And it starts with a ‘W’. But the game changed along the way, and as the Oilers careened from Mikko Koskinen to Connor Ingram, from Mike Smith to Stuart Skinner, we realized that perhaps it was an environment issue in Edmonton as much as it was about the quality of the netminders. Well, after consecutive games where an Oilers goalie was the best player on the ice, Edmonton might finally have something here. Tristan Jarry stopped 30 shots, Evan Bouchard scored the OT winner, and for the second straight game the visitors were the better team yet lost, as the Oilers beat the Philadelphia Flyers 3-2. “Good teams ... what they do is find ways to win,” said head coach Mike Babcock. “They rely on their structure even when it's a disaster. You're five tight (around the net) and doing good things. “Jars made tons of good saves, but he didn't have to go east-west a ton. There weren't lateral feeds ... the (shot attempts) were coming right at him. As bad as we were we still did OK that way.” When the 27th-place team comes into your building and spanks you as badly as the Flyers did the Oilers — as of this morning, the No. 1 team in the NHL with 31 points in 20 games — it can’t all be good, however. items.summary: The only thing missing from Zayne Parekh’s goal-of-the-year candidate was, um, the goal. Otherwise, he would have been a frontrunner.

items.body: Rangers goalie shows off agility, uses glove to rob Parekh of wraparound goal Joonas Korpisalo had to make a split-second decision: Stick or no stick? The New York Rangers goalie chose no stick, so he tossed his twig and dove across the crease to make an impressive save with his glove. Early in the first period of Wednesday’s matchup between the Rangers and the Calgary Flames at the Scotiabank Saddledome, Korpisalo robbed Flames defenseman Zayne Parekh of what would’ve been a beautiful goal. As Parekh made his push towards the net, deking multiple defenders on his way, he skated behind the goal and had an open look at a wraparound with Korpisalo set up on the far side of the crease. But Korpisalo recognized Parekh’s move around the back of the net, dropped his stick, and used his freed glove to swat the puck out of harms way. items.summary: Ilya Safonov had only four assists in 12 AHL games with Vancouver’s minor-league affiliate, the Abbotsford Canucks.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: David Kirouac-Imagn Images The Vancouver Canucks announced Wednesday that forward Ilya Safonov was placed on unconditional waivers for the purpose of contract termination. The news comes one day after Safonov’s agent, Dan Milstein, confirmed to Daily Faceoff Vancouver/Canucks Army that his client left the Canucks’ American Hockey League affiliate, the Abbotsford Canucks, to head back to Russia to play in the KHL. “Ilya valued his time with the Canucks organization and built strong relationships with the coaching and development staff in Abbotsford,” Milstein said Tuesday. “While he did not reach his goal of playing in the NHL, he leaves grateful for the opportunity and will always look back on his time in Vancouver fondly.” Safonov was originally drafted by the Chicago Blackhawks in the sixth round of the 2021 NHL Entry Draft. He was traded to the Canucks after the 2024-25 season, then signed a one-year, two-way contract with Vancouver last summer. But 12 games into the North American portion of his professional career, he has just four assists with Abbotsford. Safonov, a native of Moscow, had 16 goals and 17 assists for 33 points in 68 games with Kazan Ak-Bars in the KHL. He also had two goals and seven assists for nine points in 20 Gagarin Cup games. His best season came in 2022-23, he posted a career-high 19 goals and 18 assists for 37 points and was named a KHL All-Star. Through seven KHL seasons, he had 65 goals and 63 assists for 128 points in 331 regular-season games. He also had 10 goals and 16 assists for 26 points in 79 playoff games.

items.body: Add to Preferred Sources The Chicago Blackhawks have been arguably the biggest disappointment in the NHL this season, and general manager Kyle Davidson knows it. Granger’s update suggests the Golden Knights will activate Wotherspoon from the long-term injured reserve ahead of tonight’s contest against the Utah Mammoth. Vegas acquired Wotherspoon in a trade with the Pittsburgh Penguins this past offseason. The 29-year-old blueliner signed a two-year, $2MM contract with the Penguins a year before. The Golden Knights had to part with Kaedan Korczak , who recently signed a four-year, $13MM ($3.25MM AAV) extension, to acquire Wotherspoon. Still, since Pittsburgh ate 50% of Wotherspoon’s salary ($500K), Vegas eagerly made the swap. Unfortunately, because of his upper-body ailment, Wotherspoon’s hasn’t been able to build on last year’s success. In 80 games with the Penguins, Wotherspoon scored three goals and 30 points with a +17 rating, while averaging 20:10 of ice time per game. The Surrey, BC, native also blocked 112 shots and delivered 162 hits, making him a high-value two-way defenseman with his relatively low salary. The multi-week upper-body injury has limited him to six games with his new club. He’s gone scoreless in those six contests, with a -6 rating and a dismal 82.1% on-ice SV%. Still, if he stays healthy, Wotherspoon has 65 more regular-season contests to have a strong year heading into unrestricted free agency. items.body: TORONTO — When I sat down to write about the Toronto Maple Leafs today, reflecting on how people thought the season might go and how it’s gone, the first thing I did was search for this old tweet: It’s a Hall of Fame tweet, and relevant for a Leafs convo. There are haters celebrating today. Still, I was not in the haters camp. I liked some of the adds (Darren Raddysh has been great), was neutral on others, was excited about Gavin McKenna, and thought a guy like Easton Cowan would have more to give. Hell, I like Nick Paul and thought Brandon Duhaime would be a jolt of energy. I was, however, unsure about Sergei Bobrovsky . Because I watch this team all year, I was hopeful I’d be wrong — it’s more fun to watch a winner — but it felt like a questionable bet and, at this point, it’s not going great. So, we’re 20 games in and the Leafs are in the midst of a losing streak. They’re 1-6 in their last seven, and they play two of the league’s three best teams in their next two games. What showed up early as faint cracks are splitting. That said, I’m here to zag: better days are ahead. The Leafs are not a .450 winning percentage team, which last season would’ve finished as the third-worst points percentage in the NHL, below the actual 2025-26 Leafs, who drafted first overall after finishing 28th. They’re better still than a .500 team, but last year it would’ve taken a .580 points percentage to make playoffs in the East (Ottawa cleared that bar as the eighth seed with a .604) and .525 would’ve done it in the West. items.title: Senators’ Nick Cousins out at least a week after Chychrun hit
items.summary: Cousins exited Tuesday night’s game after taking a huge hit from the Capitals defender.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Marc DesRosiers-Imagn A notable update after a massive collision on Tuesday night. When speaking to the media on Wednesday, Ottawa Senators head coach Travis Green revealed that forward Nick Cousins will miss at least a week to 10 days after taking a huge hit from Washington Capitals defenseman Jakob Chychrun. The play that put Cousins on the shelf came late in the third period at Canadian Tire Center. Cousins was looking to break the puck out of the Ottawa zone, but was leveled by Chychrun, who was pinching in from the left point. The hit sent Cousins soaring into the glass before falling flat to the ice. Cousins was left motionless on the ice before receiving assistance from the Senators’ training staff. He was taken off the ice and immediately brought to the team’s dressing room. He didn’t return to the game. No penalty was called on the play. Green confirmed what many who saw the hit believed, and that was the fact that Cousins was knocked out on the ice after the check. Tuesday night’s contest was Cousin’s 19th appearance of the 2026-27 season. The veteran center has struggled to find his offensive touch, scoring just two goals and three points thus far. He has a plus/minus of -5 while averaging 9:45 of ice time, amassing 44 penalty minutes. The Senators wrap up their quick home swing on Thursday night, hosting the Colorado Avalanche. Ottawa (11-6-2) sits fourth in the Atlantic Division, holding the first Wild Card spot in the Eastern Conference.

items.title: Canadian government official confirms visa denial of Russian players for 2027 World Juniors
items.summary: Prime Minister Mark Carney previously stated that Russians wouldn’t be playing in the upcoming tournament.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Canada is digging in its heels about allowing Russia to play in Alberta next month. According to TSN’s Gord Miller, the Canadian government has told both Hockey Canada and the International Ice Hockey Federation it will not issue visas to Russian players seeking to play in the upcoming IIHF World Junior Championship. Also, players who might already have visas – players in the Canadian Hockey League – are considered ineligible to participate, even if it was under a neutral flag. This comes not long after Canadian prime minister Mark Carney stated that Russia “will not” be at the World Juniors, which are set to begin on Dec. 26 in Edmonton and Red Deer. The whole debate on whether Russia would be allowed to play in the upcoming event came after the Court of Arbitration for Sport ruled that the Russian Ice Hockey Federation must be allowed to compete in IIHF events, citing that the IIHF didn’t provide enough evidence to keep the ban on Russian teams in place. The IIHF, along with numerous international hockey federations, has voiced its displeasure on the decision. Nations have come forward, stating that they won’t play Russia in any international events, with some big-time sponsors threatening to pull their funding from the IIHF, if Russia is allowed to compete. As it stands, Norway, the last-ranked team heading into the WJC, has been informed that it will be removed from the tournament to make way for Russia . However, many expect Russia to be forced to back out, leading to Norway’s readmission to the event. The ban on Russian hockey teams dates back to 2022, when the nation invaded Ukraine shortly after the Beijing Olympics.

items.title: Senators’ Cousins out at least one week after hit from Capitals’ Chychrun
items.body: Nick Cousins won't be back on the ice for the next little while. The Ottawa Senators enforcer is out at least one week after absorbing a massive hit from Washington Capitals defenceman Jakob Chychrun on Tuesday, head coach Travis Green told reporters Wednesday. Cousins was briefly knocked out by the play, Green said. No penalty was called. Washington went on to win 3-2 in overtime. As Cousins looked to clear the puck out of the defensive end late in the third period, Chychrun caught him with his head down and sent him flying into the boards. Cousins stayed face-down on the ice before eventually getting to his feet and making his way off the ice with assistance from teammates. He did not return. "He's not doing great," Green said after the game, adding that Cousins did not go to the hospital. "I thought it was a head shot to a player who wasn't ready for it. They must have saw it different." The officials reviewed the hit for a five-minute major, but determined there was no penalty. "I should be careful what I say; I don't like seeing that stuff," Senators forward Ridly Greig said. Added captain Thomas Chabot: "I hate, I think everybody hates, these scenes in hockey, in any sport." Cousins, 33, has two goals and one assist in 19 games this season. The Senators are back in action Thursday at home against the Colorado Avalanche.

Subsequent reports from multiple insiders, including ESPN’s Emily Kaplan, indicated that if Michkov did indeed want a trade, his camp had not lodged that request directly with the Flyers’ management staff. Now, according to Sportsnet NHL insider Frank Seravalli , Flyers general manager Daniel Briere has no plans to trade Michkov to another team. “This is all news to me… We’ve never discussed that.” Briere told Seravalli. “He’s got so much ahead of him that we’re all really excited about. items.title: Mercer stepped up for Jets in game about Hellebuyck
items.summary: Mercer scored two goals as the Jets beat the Devils in Connor Hellebuyck’s return game that wasn’t.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect There was a big revenge game in the Canada Life Centre on Tuesday night, but it wasn’t star goalie Connor Hellebuyck beating his old team as a member of the New Jersey Devils . On Wednesday’s episode of Daily Faceoff LIVE , host Tyler Yaremchuk and co-host and former NHL video coach Steve Peters discussed Mercer’s impactful performance on a cathartic night for the Jets and their fans. items.body: Saw Carolina play as a 13-year-old, now facing Kraken in Global Series HELSINKI -- Sebastian Aho is living a dream that took shape 16 years ago. He was 13 years old and found himself at Hartwall Arena -- the mecca of Finnish hockey and home to the Finnish national ice hockey team -- to watch the Carolina Hurricanes take on the Minnesota Wild in the 2010 NHL Premiere Series. The trip from his home in Oulu to the Finnish capital is about seven hours by car, but for Aho it may as well have been a different world. He sat in the stands wide-eyed and imagined himself in the NHL, imagined one day being like the Finnish NHL players in the game below -- Mikko Koivu and Antti Miettinen from the Wild and Jussi Jokinen , Joni Pitkanen , and Tuomo Ruutu from the Hurricanes. When the 2026 NHL Global Series Finland takes place on Thursday, Aho will stand on that same ice, in what is now called Veikkaus Arena, as one of the faces of the Hurricanes, who are the defending Stanley Cup champion. He will be the focal point of the sold-out crowd, including a contingent of youth players from Oulu that is making the trek for the two games against the Seattle Kraken, the first on Thursday (12 p.m. ET; HHN, Prime Video, CARNHL, KONG, NHLN, SN+, TVAS) and second on Saturday (1 p.m. ET; HHN, Prime Video, CARNHL, KONG, KING, NHLN, SN1). “It's so cool,” Aho told NHL.com. “I mean there's a lot of friends and family at those games and that's obviously special, but I was in the game in 2010 when Canes played the Wild and I do remember it was amazing. “You can watch more NHL games live in Europe and get more highlights and stuff like that now than you could before, but it brings it that much closer when you are there in the building. It's cool to see all of it, the show and high-pace, high-level hockey.

items.title: Briere says Flyers have no plan to trade Michkov
items.summary: The message from Daniel Briere was clear: The Flyers have no intention of moving Matvei Michkov.
items.body: TORONTO — Despite a report about Matvei Michkov’s apparent unhappiness and potential interest in a change of scenery, the Philadelphia Flyers say they have not received a request for a trade from Michkov’s agent and were surprised by the news. “This is all news to me,” Flyers general manager Daniel Briere said. Beyond that, the message from Briere was clear: The Flyers have no intention of moving Michkov. “No, that’s not the plan at all,” Briere said. “We’ve never discussed that.” The report from NHL Network ’s Kevin Weekes cited “internal turmoil” with the Flyers as part of Michkov’s interest in “wanting a new start elsewhere,” but earlier on Wednesday following the GM Meetings in downtown Toronto, Briere took zero issue with Michkov’s emotion that spilled over to the bench during an in-game confrontation with teammate Nick Seeler. “I actually like the fact that our guys are fiery and they want to win,” Briere said. “That’s what I saw [in Vancouver]. It’s showing competitive players. That’s what we’re looking for, that’s what we want. The reality is, the team hasn’t performed great this year and players expect more out of themselves.” Briere scoffed at the notion that the in-game quarrelling over a sequence in the offensive zone had any indication that the Flyers were lacking in the culture department, as some observers have suggested. “If we had a culture where guys are yelling at each other and no one is responding, a culture that guys don’t care about winning, then we’d be in trouble,” Briere said. “But when you show a culture that guys want to better themselves and they’re not happy where they are, I expect that.” One of the most emotional and competitive players on the last great Flyers teams, Briere said he was glad there weren’t as many cameras as there are now.

After Tuesday night's 6-3 loss to the Colorado Avalanche, the Maple Leafs are 8-10-2 and on pace for 76 points — two fewer points than they finished with last season. And that's in an 84-game season. It was after their fourth straight loss at home — and their sixth loss in seven games — that Toronto Maple Leafs coach Jim Hiller was asked what's behind his team's recent slump. Was it injuries? Untimely giveaways? Underachieving performances from the stars? More Videos "I don't want to make excuses," said Hiller, who doesn't seem to have any answers these days. "Our record is what it is. It's deserved. I think we could have a better record, but we don't." Maybe (just maybe), the Leafs aren't good enough. Or maybe they aren't as good as some may have thought they would be after what was an aggressive re-tool this past summer, which saw the team turn over more than half the roster. items.body: TORONTO -- All is quiet between the Minnesota Wild and Quinn Hughes , and the team could keep the defenseman past the NHL Trade Deadline on March 1 if he doesn’t sign a new deal, general manager Bill Guerin said Tuesday. Hughes, whom the Wild acquired from the Vancouver Canucks in a trade Dec. 12, 2025, is in the final season of a six-year, $47.1 million contract ($7.85 million average annual value) he signed with Vancouver on Oct. 3, 2021. The 27-year-old has been eligible to sign a new contract with the Wild since July 1. If he doesn’t sign before June 30, he will become an unrestricted free agent the next day. On Oct. 24, Hughes said he “wouldn’t be surprised if something happens soon.” But Tuesday, Guerin said the situation is “status quo.” “Because, honestly, I just want him to focus on hockey,” Guerin said. “Like I said, he knows what’s going on in his head. He understands everything.” Would Guerin be willing to keep Hughes past the trade deadline? Hughes won the Norris Trophy as the NHL’s best defenseman in 2024. Since the trade, Hughes has 80 points (11 goals, 69 assists) in 68 games, second on the Wild and second among NHL defensemen. In that span, forward Kirill Kaprizov leads Minnesota with 87 points (44 goals, 43 assists) in 67 games, and Evan Bouchard of the Edmonton Oilers is first among NHL defensemen with 98 points (26 goals, 72 assists) in 70 games. The Wild (13-3-4), who extended their point streak to nine games (7-0-2) with a 2-1 overtime win at the Montreal Canadiens on Tuesday, lead the Central Division. “Honestly, we’re a better team with Quinn Hughes, so I mean, I want to keep him as long as I possibly can,” Guerin said. “Whether it’s three months, three years, seven years, whatever, we’re a better team with Quinn Hughes.”

Boo birds flew as the win probability evaporated and the home team lost by multiple goals, for the third time in as many games. Tuesday’s 6-3 defeat by the Colorado Avalanche dropped Toronto’s homestand record to 0-4. They’ve been outscored 17-7 over this span. And their record through 20 games is worse than it was at this point last season, when they tumbled to 28th overall and found themselves just bad enough to win the draft lottery. Naturally, the spirit of a group riding high and fresh out of training camp has taken a hit. Frustration is creeping in. You can hear it in the tone of the coach and in the words of the players after their sixth regulation loss in seven tries. “Of course. You don’t ever like to lose one . items.title: Mercer scores twice as Jets beat Hellebuyck-less Devils
items.body: Former Devils forward Dawson Mercer and Kyle Connor each scored twice to lead the Winnipeg Jets to an emotional 4-2 victory over New Jersey on Tuesday. The victory extended Winnipeg's win streak to four games, and halted New Jersey’s at five games. Former Devils netminder Nico Daws made 19 saves for Winnipeg (8-8-3) before a capacity crowd of 15,321 fans at Canada Life Centre. After Mercer gave the Jets a 3-2 lead on the power play at 11:58 of the third period, Connor sealed the outcome with an unassisted empty-net goal. The Devils, who trailed 2-0 after the first period, tied the game in the second period with a pair of goals 44 seconds apart. Bratt scored at 1:14 on a perfect setup from Arseny Gritsyuk from behind the net. Jack Hughes also assisted to extend his point streak to six games. Glass then tied the game at 1:58 when he deflected Jonathan Kovacevic’s shot past Daws. Declan Chisholm also assisted. Connor scored during a two-man advantage at 15:06 of the first period when he deflected Cole Perfetti’s pass past Allen. Mark Scheifele also assisted, moving him into a second-place tie with Dale Hawerchuk in all-time assists in franchise history with 550. Mercer opened the scoring at 7:54 when his snap shot from the faceoff circle beat Allen. Jets: Came out energized by the crowd booing and chanting, “Helle Sucks!” to express their anger that former Jets goalie Connor Hellebuyck did not start against Winnipeg in their first game against the Devils since the Jets traded him to New Jersey. They jumped to a 2-0 lead. Devils: Took the wind out of the Jets’ sails by scoring two goals 44 seconds apart early in the second period to tie the game 2-2. But they failed to score after that. It took the Devils 13 minutes before they got a shot on net in the third period.

items.body: The Ottawa Senators had one of their better performances of the season on Tuesday but still ended up in the loss column. The Senators (11-6-2) outworked, outmuscled and outshot the Washington Capitals but couldn’t outscore the visitors, falling 3-2 in overtime. The bright side was the fact they still managed to earn a point. The Senators have been without starting goaltender Linus Ullmark for almost three weeks but have managed to hold their own and play some impressive hockey. The Senators have gone 4-3-2 without Ullmark, thanks in large part to 27-year-old Samuel Ersson of Sweden, who seems to be finding his game, and the team remaining committed to smart decisions with and without the puck. Tuesday was a perfect example. Washington scored on its first shot and outshot Ottawa 11-5 in the opening 20 minutes. From the start of the second, the Senators dominated and outshot the Capitals 17-2 — holding the American squad without a shot for more than 21 minutes. “I thought we played awesome tonight,” said Senators head coach Travis Green. “It was one of our better games of the year.” Not one to be lavish in his praise, Green said he liked everything about his team’s game. “Thought we checked well,” he said. “We created a lot. items.title: Hellebuyck says concerns for family, uncertain career path made him ask Jets for trade
items.summary: WINNIPEG -- Connor Hellebuyck said his family’s safety and uncertainly about his career played a part in requesting a trade from the Winnipeg Jets at the end of last season.
items.body: Devils goalie reiterates love for Winnipeg, but some things ‘crossed the line’ WINNIPEG -- Connor Hellebuyck said his family’s safety and uncertainly about his career played a part in requesting a trade from the Winnipeg Jets at the end of last season. But the New Jersey Devils goalie would not point to one thing that made him decide to ask out. “There’s no one singular moment that wasn’t important in all of this decision-making and this is over a span of time,” Hellebuyck said in his return to Canada Life Centre on Tuesday. “I will say with all the uncertainty I was experiencing, there was some moments and some things that happened to my family that for me crossed the line. And as a husband and a father, I felt made that decision very certain, that I needed to be a good husband and a good father and do what’s best for my family and my career.” Hellebuyck, who was traded by the Jets to the Devils on Oct. 23, was addressing the Winnipeg media for the first time since his exit interview April 17, after the Jets failed to qualify for the Stanley Cup Playoffs. items.title: Senators’ Cousins exits after big hit from Capitals’ Chychrun
items.body: The Ottawa Senators went down a forward late in Tuesday's game against the Washington Capitals . Nick Cousins was forced to exit the game after he was on the receiving end of a massive hit from Capitals defenceman Jakob Chychrun with three minutes remaining in the third period. As Cousins was looking to clear the puck out of the defensive end, Chychrun caught the Senators forward with his head down and sent him flying into the boards. Cousins stayed face down on the ice before eventually getting to his feet and making his way off the ice with assistance from teammates. He would not return for the remainder of the game. "He's not doing great," head coach Travis Green said after the game . The officials reviewed the hit for a five-minute major, but determined that there was no penalty on the hit.

items.body: Fresh off Hockey Hall of Fame initiation, former Canadiens goalie honored in front of home crowd MIN@MTL: Price gets ovations on joining Canadiens' Ring of Honor It took four minutes for the fans at the Bell Centre to get back in their seats after Carey Price took the ice. The former Montreal Canadiens goaltender – and now a member of the 2026 Hockey Hall of Fame class – was honored on Tuesday at the arena he called home for his entire 15-year NHL career. As he was introduced, fans gave him a standing ovation which lasted four whole minutes before he addressed the crowd. Chants of “Carey! Carey!” and “Ole! Ole!” rang out as Price took it all in. L'ovation debout de quatre minutes la plus méritée de l'histoire The most well-deserved four-minute standing ovation #GoHabsGo | @CP0031 pic.twitter.com/ehAzCiXF0Z Tuesday’s addition to the Canadiens’ Ring of Honour comes a day after Price’s induction into the Hockey Hall of Fame on Monday in Toronto. Price – the Canadiens’ all-time winningest goalie – was drafted by Montreal in the first round of the 2005 NHL Draft, making his debut with the team in the 2007 season. He played his entire career with the Canadiens until his retirement in 2022. He finished his career with a 361-261-79 record and a .917 save percentage with 49 shutouts. In his career-defining 2014-15 season, Price swept the individual NHL awards, winning the William M. Jennings Trophy, Vezina Trophy, Ted Lindsay Award and the Hart Memorial Trophy. He added the Bill Masterton Memorial Trophy in the 2021-22 season.
